authors: Sumit Saha, Steven Linforth, Nandakishor Desai, Tuan Ngo
title: Spectrally Normalised Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Imputation Network with Gradient Penalty and Two Timescale Update Rule for Structural Health Monitoring
validity_discussion: The paper explicitly incorporates Rubin's combining rules for multiple imputation to quantify point estimates, within/between-imputation variance, and confidence intervals. Key quote: "For multiple imputation with SN-WGAIN-GP, we apply Rubin's combining rules [13] to derive point estimates and confidence intervals that account for imputation uncertainty in damage detection."

authors: Dawei Liu, Hanne I. Oberman, Johanna Muñoz, Jeroen Hoogland, Thomas P.A. Debray
title: Quality control, data cleaning, imputation
validity_discussion: Reviews statistical validity in real-world healthcare data, detailing how single imputation distorts sampling variability and outlining Rubin's rules for pooling multiple imputations to reflect within- and between-imputation uncertainty. Key quote: "Pooling results across multiple imputed datasets is not trivial and typically requires to consider three sources of uncertainty... These equations are also known as Rubin's rules (34,77,78)..."

authors: Zachary K. Collier, Kamal Chawla, Olushola Soyoye
title: Optimizing Imputation for Educational Data: Exploring Training Partition and Missing Data Ratios
validity_discussion: Evaluates statistical validity in propensity score analysis under Rubin's framework, assessing covariate balance, Type I error rates, and relative bias of standard errors (RBSE) across MICE machine learning methods. Key quote: "According to Rubin's combination rules, the estimates are combined in the combination phase, and confidence intervals are obtained (Little & Rubin, 2019)."

authors: Ricardo Cardoso Pereira, Pedro Henriques Abreu, Pedro Pereira Rodrigues
title: Partial Multiple Imputation With Variational Autoencoders: Tackling Not at Randomness in Healthcare Data
validity_discussion: Discusses missing data mechanisms (MCAR, MAR, MNAR) and explicitly contrasts its partial MI latent vector averaging approach with standard Rubin multiple imputation. Key quote: "We denote this procedure as a partial MI strategy since for it to be a standard MI the N results from the sampling process need to be independently analyzed before the aggregation, which is not applicable in this context."

title: The MIDAS Touch: Accurate and Scalable Missing-Data Imputation with Deep Learning
validity_discussion: Provides detailed discussion of Rubin's multiple imputation framework, valid inference, and uncertainty representation across M independently imputed datasets without joint distribution assumptions. Key quote: "The most widely used of these techniques, multiple imputation (MI), involves replacing each missing element with several values that preserve relationships within the observed data while representing uncertainty about the correct imputation model."

title: Neural Network Imputation in Complex Survey Design
validity_discussion: Addresses inferential validity in complex survey designs, deriving total weighted variance by combining complete-case variance and neural network imputation variance within Rubin's MI framework. Key quote: "Multiple imputation (MI), as proposed by Rubin [31], replaces the missing value by a vector of imputed values to obtain a number of complete datasets... The total variance is then a weighted sum of these two variance components [23]."
